developers.title: Developer documentation
developers.lead: Build on Thapsus-HR with a versioned REST API, signed webhooks and a typed TypeScript SDK. Every call is served from your workspace’s home region and is never cached at the edge.

authentication.title: Authentication
authentication.body: Use a scoped API key (thr_sk_…) or an OAuth 2.0 client: POST /v1/oauth/token with grant_type=client_credentials and HTTP Basic authentication returns a bearer token (thr_at_…) valid for an hour. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

scopes.title: Scopes and roles
scopes.body: Each credential has a role and scopes. It can do only what both allow. Credentials never reach sign-in, settings or security endpoints.

pagination.title: Pagination
pagination.body: List endpoints take ?limit and ?cursor and return { data, nextCursor }. Pass nextCursor back until it is null. Cursors are opaque.

idempotency.title: Idempotency
idempotency.body: Send an Idempotency-Key header on POST and PATCH. Repeating the same request with the same key returns the stored response (Idempotent-Replayed: true) for 24 hours; a different request with the same key is refused with 422.

rateLimits.title: Rate limits
rateLimits.body: Limits apply per workspace per minute. Every response carries RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset; over the limit you get 429 with Retry-After.

webhooks.title: Webhooks and signatures
webhooks.body: Each delivery carries Thapsus-Signature: t=<time>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "t.body">. Verify it with your signing secret, reject timestamps older than five minutes and de-duplicate on Thapsus-Event-Id. The SDK’s verifyWebhookSignature does this for you.

versioning.title: Versioning
versioning.body: The API is versioned in the path (/v1). Additive changes ship within a version. Deprecated operations send Deprecation, Sunset and Link headers at least six months before removal.

residency.title: Data residency
residency.body: Call the API in your home region (api.uk, api.eu or api.us). Webhooks and audit streams are sent from your home region to destinations you choose.

billing.title: Billing
billing.regionNote: Your billing details and invoices are stored in {region}.
billing.ownersOnly: Only the company owner can manage billing.

billing.invoiceCollection: Paid by invoice, due within {days} days. PO number: {po}

billing.currencyLocked: The currency is fixed once a paid subscription has started.

pricing.trialBadge: Free for {days} days, no card needed

core.name: Core

plus.name: Plus

enterprise.name: Enterprise

trial.title: Free trial

monthly.title: Monthly rolling

currency.title: Currency
currency.body: Pay in pounds, euros or US dollars. Your currency is set when your first paid subscription starts.

meta.description: Live status of Thapsus-HR in the United Kingdom, the European Union and the United States.

statusPage.title: Service status

tenants.allLead: Every region, from the global directory: identifiers, regions, plan and status only.

plans.title: Plans and contracts

plans.discounts: Annual discount {annual}. Discount codes: {codes}. Free trial: {trial} days.

contracts.endConfirm: End this contract? Billing stops at the end of its end date.
contracts.newLead: Custom prices are stored on the contract record. Activating it bills each of the customer's billing accounts by invoice.

status.title: Status page

audit.title: Staff audit trail

settings.title: Support contact channels

meta.title: Security and trust — Thapsus-HR
meta.description: Where your data lives, how it is protected, our sub-processors and how we handle privacy.

hero.title: Your people’s data, kept close and kept safe
hero.lead: Choose where your data lives. We keep it there, encrypt it, isolate it from every other customer and give you the tools to meet your own privacy obligations.

residency.title: Data stays in the region you choose
residency.lead: At sign-up you choose the United Kingdom, the European Union or the United States. Records, files, backups, logs, search indexes, caches, queues and emails stay there.
residency.backupHome: Backups stay in the same region, across availability zones
residency.global: A small global service only knows which region your workspace lives in. It holds no employee personal data.

isolation.title: Isolated from other customers
isolation.body: Every table is protected by database row-level security, proven by automated tests on every change.

encryption.title: Encrypted everywhere
encryption.body: TLS in transit and encryption at rest with keys held in each region’s key management service.

vault.title: Sensitive data in a separate vault
vault.body: Health, sickness, diversity and immigration data are encrypted field by field and every access is logged.

access.title: Strong sign-in
access.body: Multi-factor authentication for administrators, single sign-on, session timeouts and lockout.

audit.title: Append-only audit trail
audit.body: Every change and every view of sensitive data is recorded in a tamper-evident log you can export.

backups.title: Resilient backups
backups.body: Continuous backups in your region. After deletion, backups expire automatically within {days} days.

privacy.title: Privacy tools for your team
privacy.lead: You are the controller of your HR data. These tools help you meet your obligations.

dsr.title: Data subject requests
dsr.body: Access exports, corrections and erasure, with legal deadlines for UK GDPR, GDPR and CCPA.

retention.title: Retention
retention.body: Statutory minimums per country with sources, your own policies, dry runs and a deletion log.

export.title: Export everything
export.body: Download all of your company’s data at any time, with a manifest and checksums.

closure.title: Verified deletion
closure.body: Close your account with a {grace}-day grace period, then receive a deletion certificate.

incidents.title: Incident and breach log
incidents.body: Deadlines such as the 72-hour regulator notice, with reminders before they pass.

dpa.title: Legal terms

note.headcountDefinition: Headcount counts everyone employed on the date, including people on their last day, grouped by the job record in force that day.
note.monthEnds: One point per month end; the last point is the end of the period.
note.restricted: Some values are hidden by your access rights and are shown as restricted.
note.turnoverMethod: Turnover = leavers in the period ÷ average of the headcounts on the first and last day × 100.
note.absenceMethod: Approved absence overlapping the period, in working days of each person's work pattern, excluding public holidays. Annual leave and time off in lieu are not included.
note.bradford: Bradford factor = spells² × days over the 52 weeks to the end of the period (enabled in report settings).
note.liabilityMethod: Leave earned but not taken by the date, valued at contractual basic pay: annual pay ÷ (52 × working days per week).
note.liabilityRounding: Amounts are calculated in whole minor units and rounded once, half away from zero. Over-taken leave shows as a negative amount.
note.overtimeMethod: Approved timesheets for weeks starting in the period.
note.truncated: Only the first rows are shown. Export the report to get every row.
note.complianceAggregates: Sex and self-identification data stay encrypted in the vault; only totals from the compliance centre are shown. Each decrypt is logged.
note.suppressed: Small counts are withheld (—) so that no one can be identified.
note.payTransparencyInterpretation: Indicators follow Article 9 of Directive (EU) 2023/970 as interpreted pending national law.
note.complianceStatus: Right-to-work, Form I-9 and compliance matrix status on the date, as on the compliance dashboard.

exports.title: Data exports
exports.intro: Send data to your own storage on a schedule: an Amazon S3 bucket in your home region ({region}) or an SFTP server. Rows and fields follow the permissions of the person who set up the export.
exports.addDestinationBody: S3 buckets must be in your home region ({region}). SFTP servers are identified by their host key.
exports.name: Name
exports.roleArnHint: A role in your AWS account whose name starts with {prefix}. Add the external ID shown after saving to its trust policy.
exports.trustHint: Use this external ID in your role's trust policy. The admin guide has the exact policy.
exports.hostKeyHint: The server's SHA256 fingerprint, for example from ssh-keyscan piped to ssh-keygen -lf -. Connections to a server with a different key are refused.
exports.secretsEncrypted: Passwords and keys are encrypted with your region's key and are never shown again.
